guide.summary: Archaeology, chapels, catacombs and museums, with pizzerias, historic cafés, pastry shops and hotel rooftop bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Book the Cappella Sansevero before you go: reservations are mandatory, online tickets go on sale 60 days ahead, and the chapel is closed on Tuesdays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Gallerie d'Italia and Pizzeria Brandi are closed on Mondays, Cappella Sansevero and MADRE on Tuesdays, and the Catacombe di San Gennaro on Wednesdays.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Cappella Sansevero and the Catacombe di San Gennaro both require booking, and Sansevero releases tickets 60 days ahead. Pompeii tickets carry your name, with a cap of 20,000 entries a day.

toolkit.label: Walk-in policies
toolkit.copy: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele and the Sky Lounge Bar at the Grand Hotel Vesuvio take no reservations. Mimì alla Ferrovia seats parties of one to three in arrival order and books groups of four to ten online.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Pompeii admits only small bags up to 30x30x15 cm, and Cappella Sansevero bans photos, video and phone use. Caruso Roof Garden and George Restaurant ask for smart casual, and George welcomes children over 5.

guide.dek: Book Sansevero, the catacombs and Pompeii ahead, then leave room for walk-in pizza and a rooftop drink.
intro: In Naples, a good plan starts with booking rules. At the Museo Cappella Sansevero on Via Francesco De Sanctis, booking is mandatory, online tickets go on sale 60 days ahead, and the chapel opens 9:00–19:00 every day except Tuesday, with a standard ticket of €12. Photos and phone use are not allowed inside. Nearby, Pio Monte della Misericordia on Via dei Tribunali shows Caravaggio's Seven Works of Mercy, open Monday to Saturday 10:00–18:00. Napoli Sotterranea, at Piazza San Gaetano 69, runs underground tours from 10:00, plus a Thursday 21:00 tour by reservation.

For Pompeii, the winter timetable runs from 15 October to 15 March: gates open at 9:00, last entry is 15:30 and the site closes at 17:00. Tickets carry your name, entries are capped at 20,000 a day, and you may bring only small bags up to 30x30x15 cm. Pompeii Express costs €20 for the ancient city alone, while Pompeii + adds the suburban villas and a shuttle for €25. Entry is free on the first Sunday of each month, and you can enter at Piazza Esedra, Piazza Anfiteatro or Porta Marina.

Back in the city, the Gallerie d'Italia on Via Toledo opens Tuesday to Friday 10:00–19:00 and weekends until 20:00, and shows Caravaggio's Martyrdom of Saint Ursula. Its exhibition Angelica e Élisabeth. L'età delle donne pittrici runs from 6 November 2026 to 7 March 2027. MADRE, on Via Settembrini, is closed on Tuesdays. In Chiaia, Villa Pignatelli hosts Crochet Coral Reef by Margaret and Christine Wertheim until 12 April 2027, and Città della Scienza on Via Coroglio runs its immersive Dante Inferno exhibition until the end of December 2026.

For food, L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele on Via Cesare Sersale opens daily 11:00–23:00 and takes no reservations, while Pizzeria Brandi is closed on Mondays. Mimì alla Ferrovia seats small parties in arrival order and books groups of four to ten online. For an evening view, the Grand Hotel Vesuvio's Sky Lounge Bar on Via Partenope serves cocktails daily 10:30–23:00 without reservations, and its Caruso Roof Garden requires booking and smart casual dress. George Restaurant at Grand Hotel Parker's serves dinner Tuesday to Saturday.
summaryCards: Pair a booked slot at the Cappella Sansevero with an underground tour at Napoli Sotterranea and a walk-in pizza at da Michele.
Start with coffee at Gran Caffè La Caffettiera, open from 7:00, then visit the Santa Chiara cloister, which opens at 9:30 Monday to Saturday.
Check closing days: Gallerie d'Italia shuts on Mondays, Sansevero and MADRE on Tuesdays, and the catacombs on Wednesdays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several major sites could not be read and are not included: the National Archaeological Museum (MANN), the Tesoro di San Gennaro, Sfogliatelle Attanasio and the Darwin-Dohrn Museum had certificate errors; Capodimonte and the Naples zoo refused connections; Teatro di San Carlo showed a bot check; and several bars, bakeries and pizzerias had domains that did not resolve. Hours were not published for Palazzo Reale, Città della Scienza, Mimì alla Ferrovia, Palazzo Petrucci, Il Malandrino, Gambrinus, Scaturchio and Mennella. Santa Chiara's September 2026 closure notice is an image whose dates could not be read. Several places, including Napoli Sotterranea, da Michele, Di Matteo, Pio Monte, Scaturchio and Mennella, showed no 2026-dated content and are marked medium confidence.
